question: A 35-year-old man presents with chronic, insidious-onset uveitis. Slit-lamp examination reveals large, greasy keratic precipitates (KPs) on the corneal endothelium, iris nodules at the pupillary margin, and mild posterior synechiae. Which ONE of the following best characterises this presentation?

answers.text: Non-granulomatous iridocyclitis — the large KPs indicate severe acute inflammation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Large, greasy ('mutton-fat') KPs are the hallmark of GRANULOMATOUS, not non-granulomatous, iridocyclitis. Non-granulomatous disease produces fine, stellate KPs.

answers.text: Granulomatous iridocyclitis — mutton-fat KPs and iris nodules indicate a granulomatous aetiology requiring systemic workup

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Mutton-fat KPs (large, greasy precipitates composed of epithelioid cells and macrophages), iris nodules (Koeppe/Busacca), and the insidious course are classic hallmarks of granulomatous iridocyclitis. Systemic causes — sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, leprosy, syphilis — must be sought.

answers.text: Acute congestive glaucoma — the corneal changes represent corneal oedema

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Acute angle-closure glaucoma causes corneal epithelial oedema (Descemet's folds), not discrete keratic precipitates. The iris nodules and the clinical context point clearly to granulomatous uveitis.

answers.text: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis — characterised by large mutton-fat KPs and nodules

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Fuchs heterochromic cyclitis characteristically produces fine, stellate, diffusely distributed KPs — not mutton-fat KPs. Its hallmark is heterochromia iridis (the affected eye is lighter), not iris nodules.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the KP morphology distinction: fine stellate KPs → non-granulomatous; large greasy (mutton-fat) KPs → granulomatous. Granulomatous disease carries specific systemic associations.
Well done. Mutton-fat KPs + iris nodules + insidious onset = granulomatous iridocyclitis — a constellation that mandates systemic investigation.
